summary: Backend + frontend regression for PackIntel v2 Food Intelligence. 40/41 backend pytest cases pass (1 skipped due to no matching legacy row). Live Groq AI reasoning verified end-to-end (Tomato & Curd returned intelligence.mode=ai, provider=Groq, model=openai/gpt-oss-120b). Fallback paths (missing key, 429/malformed JSON, invalid material selection, duplicate alternatives, unknown food + AI down) all degrade honestly to knowledge_base mode with a clear message; no 500s. Frontend: 5 demo buttons present (tomato/curd/potato/milk/biscuits), simple food-name input only (no pH/moisture/RH/respiration/MAP fields exposed), Tomato run navigates to /results with recommended-material, AI status card, food-profile provenance, cautions/warnings (chilling injury for 8°C/10d), specifications, alternatives, score breakdown, disclaimer. Back-to-analysis preserves priority. History lists 109 runs and reopens a stored snapshot correctly (shows Reopened from history · stored snapshot). Materials library shows 12/12 packaging materials. Mobile viewport 390px has no horizontal overflow, zero console errors across all pages.

minor.issue: Under rapid concurrent calls the Groq API returns HTTP 429 for gpt-oss-120b and the response silently falls back to knowledge_base mode. Behaviour is correct and honest (message says 'AI service temporarily unavailable') but rate limits may hide the AI mode during load. Not a bug; noted for context.

critical_code_review_comments: food_intelligence.recommend catches an over-broad tuple of exceptions when validating the AI selection: any non-hashable material id or missing attribute would silently disable AI. Acceptable for a graceful-degradation prototype but consider logging the specific validation failure so we can distinguish 429 vs model hallucination.

engine_input assumes fixed RH values (65/85/90). This is disclosed in assumptions, but a Fresh Produce food with transportation='high_humidity' still assumes 90% RH regardless of the actual storage_type/temperature. Consider whether ambient+high_humidity should differ from chilled+high_humidity.

image_service.receive_chunk reads the whole request body into memory up to CHUNK_SIZE and then hands it to a threadpool, but the 413 check inside the stream loop only fires after len(data) > CHUNK_SIZE; a client streaming exactly CHUNK_SIZE+1 in a single flush would still be rejected but the buffer already grew. Not a real DoS since FastAPI caps request size, but consider streaming to disk.

food_knowledge.py mixes reference bands with prose that reads like measurements ('assumes pasteurized refrigerated milk'). Copy is honest but ensure the frontend labels it 'typical reference profile' everywhere — verified on Tomato reopen screenshot.

recommend.py exposes SimpleRecommendationRequest as the public schema but the response is the classic RecommendationResponse which still contains an 'input' field with the *internal* RecommendationRequest (moisture_content/oil_content/ph). This leaks the derived-not-measured values through the API surface. Consider stripping or clearly labelling them as 'derived reference midpoints' at the API boundary.
seed_data_creation: None — used existing PostgreSQL fixtures and food KB.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Live AI is real: Tomato and Curd single-shot calls returned intelligence.mode=ai (Groq / openai/gpt-oss-120b). When running many /recommend calls back-to-back, expect Groq 429s that legitimately trigger the knowledge_base fallback — space calls out or accept fallback in assertions. All fallback correctness is covered by test_food_intelligence_fallback.py via monkeypatched groq_service.complete. The demo test asserts >=3 of 4 distinct primary materials, which holds even entirely in KB mode. Observed live runs: Tomato->Micro-Perforated Film, Curd->PP Cup with Sealed Lid, Potato->Paper-Based Ventilated Bag, Biscuits->Metallized Film, Milk->Aluminum Foil Laminate.
